_note: The tester's lines (af_heart): drives VoiceOver and the keyboard, says what she hears.

lines.t0-hello: Hello. This is the home page of [Marcelo](/mɑɹsˈɛloʊ/) [Paiva's](/pˈaɪvəz/) site, in Safari, with VoiceOver on. I'm the tester. I'll drive VoiceOver and the keyboard, and tell you what I hear.
lines.t0-goal: The goal is simple. Can someone using VoiceOver understand this page, find what they need, and use its controls, without seeing it?
lines.t0-steps: I test in six steps. First, I inspect the page structure in the code. Second, the keyboard on its own. Third, a reading pass with the screen reader, top to bottom. Fourth, jumping by headings, landmarks and links. Fifth, the controls themselves. And sixth, real tasks, start to finish.
lines.t1-open: Step one, before any screen reader: the structure in the code. I'm opening Safari's Web Inspector, and making it larger, to see what this page tells assistive technology.
lines.t1-button: This is the Set for you button. Its attributes say aria-expanded, false, and aria-controls points at the panel it opens.
lines.t1-count: That panel is marked hidden, and the four dropdowns are still inside it, in the page.
lines.t2-open: Step two, the keyboard on its own. No screen reader and no mouse, just the keys a keyboard user presses, and the focus ring that shows where I am.
lines.t2-skip: The first stop is a skip link. I'll press Return, then Tab, to see whether it really skips the header.
lines.t2-skipped: I'm on Read the writing, past the whole header. The skip link works.
lines.t2-order: Pause motion, then Set for you: the same order as on screen, and the focus ring follows every time.
lines.t2-type: It opens, and Tab takes me to the first setting, the drawings. With a dropdown focused, I can type the first letter of a choice. N, for not at all.
lines.t2-changed: The dropdown says not at all, and the drawings are gone. Now Escape.
lines.t2-escape: Escape closes the panel, and puts focus back on the button. Next, Pause motion.
lines.t2-pause: Space presses it, and the button now says pressed.
lines.t3-open: Step three, the reading pass. The home page from the top, in Safari with VoiceOver, the way someone who can't see the screen would meet it.
lines.t3-skip: The first thing it reaches is a skip link, which is a good start. Now I'll read the header one item at a time.
lines.t3-sfy: Set for you… a button, and it tells me it's collapsed. That's what I want to hear. Next item.
lines.t3-menu: It says menu… and again… and again. Four presses, and it hasn't moved past it.
lines.t3-retest: I'll go straight to Set for you.
lines.t3-next: Collapsed, the same as before. Next item.
lines.t3-pause: That's Pause motion, the next button on the screen. The silence is gone.
lines.t4-open: Step four, structural navigation. Someone using a screen reader rarely reads every item. They jump, by headings, by landmarks, and by links. First, headings.
lines.t4-headings: One level one, a level two for the latest writing, and the essays under it at level three. The outline holds, all the way down.
lines.t4-landmarks-ok: Each region is announced with a name, so I can tell them apart and jump straight to the one I want.
lines.t4-links: And links. In a list of links, each one has to make sense on its own.
lines.t4-doubled: The essays in the drawing strip read their title twice, and then the whole summary.
lines.t5-open: Step five, the controls. Finding Set for you isn't enough. It has to say what it is, what state it's in, and work from the keyboard.
lines.t5-state: Set for you, a button, collapsed.
lines.t5-expanded: When I press it, the state changes to expanded, and VoiceOver says so. Now the panel, one item at a time.
lines.t5-selects: The settings read as a sentence, and each dropdown has its own name… Drawings, Theme, Motion, Home page… with its current value first.
lines.t5-escape: And Escape closes it, and puts me back on the button, collapsed again.
lines.t6-open: Step six, a real task. I'll turn the drawings off, start to finish, with VoiceOver… and find out whether it tells me it worked.
lines.t6-found: There's the Drawings dropdown, set to calm color. I'll open it, and choose not at all.
lines.t6-stale: When I choose it, VoiceOver reads the old value… calm color.
lines.t6-ask: I'll ask again to hear what's set.
lines.t6-silent: Not at all. It worked… but nothing told me. The panel has a note about it, so I'll go and find it.
lines.t6-note: There it is. Drawings are off, and their captions go with them.
lines.t6-gone: And after See the work, VoiceOver goes straight to Latest writing. The drawings are gone for a listener too.
lines.t6-heard: There it is: drawings are off, and their captions go with them, said straight after the choice.
lines.t8-press: It's the second thing on the page, right after the skip link. I'll press it.
lines.t8-like: It starts with a picture: the front page of a magazine, the newest essays taking most of the page, and a narrower column beside them. Then it walks the layout from top to bottom.
lines.t9-describe: First, Describe this page. Does a written description of the layout help someone picture the page? Is it too long, or too short? Blind people who use a screen reader every day should tell us, on VoiceOver and on JAWS or NVDA.
lines.t9-sentence: Third, Set for you reads its settings as a sentence. Whether that feels natural, and whether the new announcements are enough, is for screen reader users, and people with cognitive or learning disabilities, to say.
lines.t9-zoom: Fifth, zoom and magnification. Zoomed in, the header stays at the top, and some text sits over moving colour. People with low vision who use zoom or a screen magnifier should try it.
lines.t9-collage: And last, the collage. Set for you can turn the home page into a field of drawings. This pass tested the list only.
lines.t9-close: That's the end of the first pass. Five problems found on the page: three fixed and live, one fix in review, and one still open.
lines.t4-after: Now each essay says its title once, then its summary.
lines.t8-opened: It says the dialog's name, The home page, and its heading… and stops there. The picture of the page isn't read until I go looking.
lines.t8-heard: This time it reads the picture straight away: the front page of a magazine, the newest essays taking most of the page.
